constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.target_model: MSC 6.00AX large model: int and unsigned int are 16-bit; long is signed 32-bit; plain char is signed 8-bit; far pointers are 16:16.
constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.record_layout: off starts at signed-long 4. Every record has a 4-byte tag header. P payload=12 bytes plus 10 bytes per signed nLinks; T payload=10 bytes plus 2 bytes per signed nFrames. Tags are 0x50 and 0x54. Unknown tags set off=size.
constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.byte_order: FlipWords swaps adjacent bytes for a signed-long length (calls use 12,10,10,2 and hStyl byte size). XFlipLong swaps the two words in each 20-byte StyleRun.pos after style word-byte conversion.
constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.comparisons: off<size and off<tlen-4 are signed-long comparisons using signed high and unsigned low words. Link/frame/style loops use signed 16-bit int. StyleRun.pos>=off is signed long. *q<space is signed char.
constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.pointer_rules: base+off reads far data using base.segment and base.offset+low16(off) modulo 65536; target operations preserve segment. nul-text and q-nul are same-segment signed 16-bit differences sign-extended for off/style arithmetic. tlen narrows long resource size to signed int; memory-helper lengths convert to unsigned int.
constants_widths_signedness_pointer_arit.coordinate_math: Rect and record fields are signed 16-bit ints; bitmap coordinates and text-rect translation add with 16-bit wrap. Constants: title object 0x501, window 0x502, clip window 0x500, resource kinds 0x11/0x13/10/0x15, type 1, fonts 2 and 5, record flag 1, control limit 0x20, reserved tail 4.

source_anchor.detail: compiler-generated DisplayCard frame check; exact local responsible for the 4-byte frame increase is unknown

remaining_differences.explanation: Original asks __aFchkstk for 0x76 (118) bytes; the registered candidate asks for 0x7A (122), a 4-byte compiler-frame resource delta. BEHAVIOR_EXACT_CONFIRMED assumes the ordinary valid-stack precondition that the candidate frame check succeeds (at least 122 bytes available). At 118-121 bytes the original may pass while the candidate fails; that low-stack resource boundary is explicitly outside the confirmed game-behavior domain.
Original compares i-count and uses JL; candidate compares count-i and uses JG. Both signed 16-bit comparisons branch exactly when i<nFrames.

Five pointer calculations reorder the 16-bit addition but compute the same base.offset+low16(off) modulo 65536 and keep base.segment. The diagnostic extra/missing instructions are reordered add/load operations.

root_review.basis: Reviewed the whole-function branch/call/state/width maps, source/evidence identities, explanations of residue and differential/negative limits. Matching observed service boundaries are composed through the actual caller ABI and same callee/slot/state; finite coverage alone is not acceptance.
root_review.note: The compiler-generated frame check asks for 122 versus 118 bytes. This is a compiler resource requirement, explicitly requiring sufficient stack for the candidate; the 118–121-byte resource boundary differs. Full game algorithm/calls/state match. Integration must validate actual stack sufficiency; byte identity is unclaimed.
root_review.context_note: The removed lines only repeated declarations that the same file already makes at their original position. MSC 6.00AX code generation depends on the number of identifiers declared earlier in a file; the inserted blocks made nine previously exact functions inexact (PopUpInfoWindow, DrawCurBalloons, DrawSpider, PrevListLine, f_23E6_0392, win_Recalc, f_2505_0831, f_2505_08EA, f_1E57_0F8E). Without them all nine match the original bytes again and each module verifies as a whole. A /W3 compile of every changed TU reports no implicit function declaration (positive control: C4016/C4071 on an undeclared call), so no call changed its prototype view. The behaviour-reviewed definitions in these TUs are token-identical; their static source reviews stand and their differential contracts are rerun on the new objects.
